about.title: San Marcos Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Three people died in traffic collisions in San Marcos in 2025, according to public records. Behind each of those numbers is a family in a kitchen somewhere off San Marcos Boulevard or Twin Oaks Valley Road trying to figure out what comes next. If that is where you are, we're sorry. A wrongful death claim will not undo what happened, but it can address the practical weight left behind: the funeral, the paycheck that no longer arrives, the guidance a parent or partner would have given for years to come. In California, the right to bring this claim belongs first to a spouse or domestic partner and children, with certain dependents and heirs eligible in other situations, and the clock generally runs two years from the date of death. That window shrinks when a public agency is involved, which matters on state routes like SR-78 or county-maintained roads. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We listen, then connect San Marcos families with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why San Marcos Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. An independent attorney can confirm where your family stands before anything else is decided.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is much shorter when a city, county, or state agency may share responsibility. Connecting sooner protects those options.

items.title: A civil path, separate from any criminal case
items.desc: Whether or not prosecutors in San Diego County pursue charges, your family may still bring a civil action for funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. The attorney works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on SR-78 near San Marcos. Does it matter that it was a state highway?
items.answer: It can. If a government entity such as Caltrans or the county may share responsibility, California requires a formal claim to be filed on a much shorter timeline than the usual two years. An attorney can look at the collision report, the location, and the parties involved to sort out which deadlines apply. Reaching out early keeps every option open.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves on its own track, separate from anything the San Diego County District Attorney does. A criminal conviction is not required, and an acquittal does not automatically close the civil door. Your attorney can explain how the two proceedings may affect each other.

items.question: What can a wrongful death claim actually recover for our family?
items.answer: California allows recovery for funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. The specific losses depend on your relationship and circumstances, and no one can promise a particular result. An independent attorney will walk through what applies to your situation honestly.
